subject: [hw] R1 finding F10 (V19, HIGH): VSRI and VSLI keep the wrong half of the destination; test generator mirrors it
body:
File: gpu/hwcodec/emu/n2a32_neon_shift.c:172-191 (vsri/vsli), used at :655/:658. Also gpu/hwcodec/emu/test_v19/gen_vectors.py:70-80, so the package suite cannot see it (both sides use the same swapped masks).

Arm pseudocode (Arm Compiler armasm reference, VSLI and VSRI; A32/T32 Advanced SIMD):
  VSRI: "The most significant bits in the destination vector are unchanged" - the source is shifted RIGHT and inserted into the LOW bits, keeping the top `shift` bits of Vd.
        result = (Vd & ~((1 << (esize-shift)) - 1)) | (Vm >> shift)
  VSLI: "The least significant bits in the destination vector are unchanged" - the source is shifted LEFT and inserted into the HIGH bits, keeping the low `shift` bits of Vd.
        result = (Vd & ((1 << shift) - 1)) | (Vm << shift)

The code does the opposite:
  vsri: (dv & low(shift)) | (sv & high(esize-shift))        -> keeps the low bits of dv
  vsli: (dv & high(esize-shift)) | ((sv << shift) & low(esize-shift)) -> keeps the high bits of dv

Repro (my independent spot suite, encodings from llvm-mc):
  vsri.32 q0,q1,#8 = F3B80452; q0=ffffffff,0; q1=11223344,0
    current d0=112233ff; expected (Vd top 8 kept) 0xff112233.
  vsli.32 q0,q1,#8 = F2A80552; q0=ffffffff,0; q1=11223344,0
    current d0=22334400; expected (Vd low 8 kept) 0x223344ff.

Why it matters: D01 census vsli.64=20, vsli.32=15, vsri.32=12, vsri.64=7 in the vendor set; these are bitfield/colour-channel inserts where the kept half is the whole point. This is a wrong-value instruction on the hot path, not a corner.

Fix (esize/shift in bits, shift >= 1 for VSRI, 0..esize-1 for VSLI):
  vsri: return (dv & ~mask_bits(esize - shift)) | ((sv >> shift) & mask_bits(esize - shift));
  vsli: return (dv & mask_bits(shift)) | ((sv << shift) & ~mask_bits(shift));
and the same formulas in gen_vectors.py (vsri/vsli) so the suite tests the architecture rather than the implementation. Please add a case with a non-zero, non-all-ones Vd so the kept half is visible (e.g. Vd=0xffffffff is actually enough for VSRI but not for the low-bit half; use Vd=0xdeadbeef).

I will re-check when you post the fix. Other V19 checks in my spot run (vshr/vshl/vsra/vrshr/vrsra/vqshl/vqshlu/vqshrn/vqrshrun/vmovl/vaddl/vmull/vmlal/scalar vmla/vqdmulh) pass; VMOVN is V20s space, not yours.
